'''Urchin''' was a [[web analytics|web statistics analysis]] program that was developed by [[Urchin Software Corporation]]. Urchin analyzed [[web server]] [[data logging|log file]] content and displayed the [[internet traffic|traffic]] information on that [[website]] based upon the log data. Sales of Urchin products ended on March 28, 2012.<ref>{{cite web|url = http://analytics.blogspot.com/2012/01/end-of-era-for-urchin-software.html|title = The End of an Era for Urchin Software|date = January 20, 2012|first = Paul|last = Muret|publisher = Google Analytics|access-date = April 7, 2012|archive-date = April 13, 2012|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20120413093651/https://www.google.com/urchin/|url-status = live}}</ref>

Urchin software could be run in two different data collection modes: log file analyzer or hybrid. As a log file analyzer, Urchin processed web server log files in a variety of log file formats. Custom file formats could also be defined. As a hybrid, Urchin combined page tags with log file data to eradicate the limitations of each data collection method in isolation.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.advanced-web-metrics.com/blog/2007/10/07/hosted-v-software-v-hybrid-tools/|title=Hosted v Software v Hybrid tools|author=|date=October 7, 2007|website=www.Advanced-Web-Metrics.com|access-date=August 31, 2017|archive-date=October 12, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141012185057/http://www.advanced-web-metrics.com/blog/2007/10/07/hosted-v-software-v-hybrid-tools/|url-status=live}}</ref> The result was more accurate web visitor data.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.advanced-web-metrics.com/blog/2008/02/16/accuracy-whitepaper/|title=Accuracy Whitepaper for web analytics|author=|date=February 16, 2008|website=www.Advanced-Web-Metrics.com|access-date=August 31, 2017|archive-date=March 6, 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110306063003/http://www.advanced-web-metrics.com/blog/2008/02/16/accuracy-whitepaper/|url-status=live}}</ref>

Urchin became one of the more popular tools for website [[traffic analysis]], particularly with ISPs and web hosting providers. This was largely due to its scalability in performance and its pricing model.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://urchin.biz/urchin-software-corp-89a1f5292999#.c0csw4u5p|title=Urchin Software Corp. – Urchin Software Corp. Vault|author=|date=September 2, 2016|website=Urchin.biz|access-date=August 31, 2017}}</ref>
{{pic|Logo of Urchin Software Corporation.svg|Logo of Urchin Software Corporation}}
{{pic|Logo of Urchin (software).svg|Logo of the Urchin software before its acquisition by Google}}
Urchin Software Corp. was acquired by [[Google]] in April 2005, forming [[Google Analytics]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.siliconbeat.com/entries/2005/03/28/google_buying_web_analytics_company.html|title=SiliconBeat: Google buying web analytics company|website=www.SiliconBeat.com|access-date=March 8, 2016|archive-date=November 9, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161109140133/http://www.siliconbeat.com/entries/2005/03/28/google_buying_web_analytics_company.html|url-status=dead}}</ref> In April 2008, Google released Urchin 6.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://analytics.googleblog.com/2008/04/graduation-day-for-website-optimizer.html|title=Graduation Day for Website Optimizer and Urchin Software!|author=|date=April 2008|website=GoogleBlog.com|access-date=August 31, 2017|archive-date=September 1, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170901021642/https://analytics.googleblog.com/2008/04/graduation-day-for-website-optimizer.html|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.urchintools.com/urchin6/about-urchin6/urchin-vs-google-analytics|title=Urchin 6 vs. Google Analytics Comparison - Urchin Software Tools|author=|date=|website=www.UrchinTools.com|access-date=August 31, 2017}}</ref> In February 2009, Google released Urchin 6.5, integrating [[AdWords]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://analytics.googleblog.com/2009/02/urchin-65-is-now-available.html|title=Urchin 6.5 is now available|author=|date=February 2009|website=GoogleBlog.com|access-date=August 31, 2017|archive-date=September 1, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170901023647/https://analytics.googleblog.com/2009/02/urchin-65-is-now-available.html|url-status=live}}</ref> Urchin 7 was released in September 2010 and included 64-bit support, a new UI, and event tracking, among other features.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://analytics.googleblog.com/2010/09/urchin-7-64-bit-released.html|title=Urchin 7 64-bit Released!|author=|date=September 2010|website=GoogleBlog.com|access-date=August 31, 2017|archive-date=September 1, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170901022526/https://analytics.googleblog.com/2010/09/urchin-7-64-bit-released.html|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.google.com/urchin/features.html|title=Google Analytics Solutions - Marketing Analytics & Measurement – Google|author=|date=|website=www.Google.com|access-date=August 31, 2017|archive-date=December 30, 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111230183847/http://www.google.com/urchin/features.html|url-status=live}}</ref>
